candidates.title: Stable Adaptive Thinking via Advantage Shaping and Length-Aware Gradient Regulation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) achieve strong performance through extended reasoning traces, but they often exhibit overthinking behavior for low-complexity queries. Existing efforts to mitigate this issue are fundamentally limited by unstable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs and poor robustness to heterogeneous reasoning behaviors. To address these challenges, we propose a two-stage framework for stable adaptive thinking in LRMs. The framework first applies Hybrid Fine-Tuning to expose the model to both thinking and no-thinking behaviors, establishing well-conditioned initialization. It then performs adaptive reinforcement learning with Correctness-Preserving Advantage Shaping (CPAS) to avoid suppressing correct long-chain reasoning, and Length-Aware Gradient Regulation (LAGR) to stabilize optimization under severe reasoning-length heterogeneity. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B show consistent improvements over strong baselines, achieving up to +3.7/+3.6 accuracy points while reducing generated tokens by 40.6%/43.9%. Further analyses across varying problem difficulties and out-of-distribution tasks confirm the robustness and generalization of our approach.

candidates.reason: Stable Adaptive Thinkingは思考／非思考のハイブリッド微調整と長さ配慮型強化学習で過剰思考を抑え、精度を上げつつ生成トークンを約40％削減する推論効率化手法である。

candidates.title: LEAD: Length-Efficient Adaptive and Dynamic Reasoning for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large reasoning models, such as OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1, tend to become increasingly verbose as their reasoning capabilities improve. These inflated Chain-of-Thought (CoT) trajectories often exceed what the underlying problems require, wasting compute, latency, and context budgets. While introducing length-based efficiency rewards during reinforcement learning offers a natural remedy, existing methods struggle with two fundamental challenges: the optimal balance between correctness and efficiency is non-stationary throughout training, and intrinsic reasoning budgets vary drastically across problems. Relying on static reward weights and global length constraints inevitably forces a compromise between degraded accuracy and unrealized compression. To overcome these limitations, we propose LEAD (Length-Efficient Adaptive and Dynamic reasoning), a method that replaces static heuristics with online, self-adaptive mechanisms. LEAD dynamically calibrates the correctness--efficiency trade-off at each step using a Potential-Scaled Instability, directing optimization capacity to the most informative learning signal. Furthermore, it estimates an adaptive per-problem target length online based on the model's own correct rollouts, applying a symmetric efficiency reward that penalizes both overthinking and over-compression. Evaluated on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, LEAD achieves the highest accuracy and Accuracy-Efficiency Score among RL-trained efficient-reasoning methods in our matched comparisons while producing substantially shorter outputs than the base model.
candidates.reason: LEADは推論モデルの冗長なCoTを問題ごとに適応的な目標長で抑え、計算量・レイテンシ・コンテキスト予算の浪費を減らす長さ効率化手法であり、強化学習は推論効率化を目的とする内部手段である。

candidates.title: PopPy: Opportunistically Exploiting Parallelism in Python Agentic Workflows
candidates.abstract: Agentic workflows, which compose calls to ML models using a general-purpose programming language like Python, are widely used for a variety of user-facing tasks, from software engineering to enterprise automation, making their end-to-end latency a critical bottleneck. To improve their latency, developers can either manually parallelize them or use restricted agentic frameworks that cannot express or exploit all forms of parallelization. We address this by developing PopPy, a system that parallelizes external calls, e.g., AI models, in agentic workflows written in a very expressive subset of Python. PopPy combines an ahead-of-time compiler with a runtime, addressing three key challenges in extracting parallelism from Python applications: language complexity, dynamic dispatch, and variable mutation. On a set of real-world agentic workflows, PopPy achieves up to $6.7\times$ speedups in end-to-end execution time, compared to standard Python execution and several agentic frameworks, while preserving the sequential program semantics.
candidates.reason: PopPyはPython製compound AI／エージェントワークフローの外部モデル呼び出しの並列性をコンパイラとランタイムで抽出し、逐次意味論を保ちつつエンドツーエンドレイテンシを最大6.7倍改善するシステムである。

candidates.title: Dual DeltaNet: Value-Side Memory Reorganization for Linear Attention
candidates.abstract: Linear attention and state space models (SSMs) offer efficient alternatives to softmax attention by maintaining a fixed-size recurrent state, but this design requires careful management to preserve useful historical associations and limit interference. The delta rule helps reduce interference through correction of the value associated with each key, but it does not explicitly account for how related value features are distributed across the state. We observe that a state $\boldsymbol{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_k\times d_v}$ can be viewed as a bank of $d_k$ addresses storing $d_v$-dimensional values. While a key-side read $\boldsymbol{S}^\top\boldsymbol{k}$ retrieves the value associated with $\boldsymbol{k}$, a value-side read $\boldsymbol{S}\boldsymbol{e}$ aggregates addresses whose stored value features match the selector $\boldsymbol{e}$. Based on this observation, we propose Dual DeltaNet (DDN), which extends Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) with a two-sided delta rule. The key-side delta rule reads with the current key to correct its associated value, while the complementary value-side delta rule reads with selected features of the current value to reorganize the addresses it occupies. We derive a chunkwise parallel training algorithm and a rank-2 recurrence that increases arithmetic intensity during inference. Compared with KDA, GDN-2, and Mamba-3, DDN achieves the strongest overall performance across language modeling, zero-shot downstream tasks, and retrieval, while incurring modest training and inference overhead relative to KDA. Code: https://github.com/ReichtumQian/DualDeltaNet
candidates.reason: Dual DeltaNetは線形注意の固定サイズ再帰状態に対しキー側と値側の二方向デルタ則で値特徴の配置を再編し干渉を抑える注意機構で、効率的な注意・状態管理への直接貢献である。
